scope: The selected Kubinka vehicle has a tall curved rear turret hatch in two museum views. Relative shape and visible hinge ownership are observed; exact dimensions, concealed bearing/seal sections and demonstration travel are inferred. This is not a vehicle survey or a Tengxian deployment claim.

references.scope: Kubinka rear-right view: curved rectangular rear hatch, rounded lower corners, two hinges on the vehicle-left edge and one visible free-edge fitting. Publisher gallery, photographed 2022-09-25; supplements the rear not visible in the primary 2017 photograph.
Same exhibit rear-left view confirms the tall rear hatch is separate from the low side vision covers.
Museum catalogue explicitly identifies a back hatch of the turret on a different preserved Type94. Corroborates the component; does not supply Kubinka dimensions or operating limits.

inferred: The rear hatch is centered on the retained cone; its absolute size follows the current uncalibrated turret size.
Radial panel clearance, armor thickness, hidden backing/seal, hinge barrel sections, pin tilt and exact hinge stations are modeled mechanical estimates.
The visible free-edge fitting is represented closed. Its internal latch construction and release motion have not been established.
The retained 100.8 degree demonstration range is a verified modeling range, not a measured stop on the exhibit.
2022 rear views supplement the 2017 primary appearance; no photograph establishes an unchanged concealed interior between those dates.

runtimeClearance.rearHatchOpenTurretYaw: Forward zero yaw only in the modeled demonstration
runtimeClearance.basis: Actual native mesh diagnostic found 14 triangle pairs with the closed driver roof at 180 degree turret yaw / 75 degree rear opening. The interlock preserves the tested forward opening pose; it is not a claimed historical operating rule.
